elections.notes: Alwiyah Talib's first term. BN retained traditional Malay base despite national tsunami. GE14 coattails boosted turnout to 78%.

results.note: Alwiyah switched from UMNO to BERSATU post-2018. Won with 50.2%.

results.correction: CORRECTED: Candidate was Mohd Youzaimi Yusof, not 'Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid' (DAF 2026-06-29)

majority.correction: CORRECTED: 3,041 votes (Alwiyah PN over BN), not 2,285 (DAF 2026-06-29)

elections.notes: CORRECTED (DAF 2026-06-29): Alwiyah retained seat under PN banner with 50.2%. Five-cornered fight, not three. PH collapsed to 6.9% (AMANAH), not 12.4% (PKR). Low turnout (55%) favored incumbent's personal vote. BN candidate was Mohd Youzaimi Yusof, not Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid.

analysis.voteRetention: Alwiyah won twice under different banners - demonstrates strong personal vote
analysis.partySwitchImpact: 2022 result shows Alwiyah retained majority of personal vote despite switching from BN to PN
analysis.2026Implication: Critical variable: how many 2022 PN voters follow her back to BN vs. stay with PN?

2022.note: BN fielded Mohd Youzaimi Yusof against Alwiyah (PN)

analysis.2022Collapse: BN vote collapsed when Alwiyah defected to PN - shows her personal vote was BN's backbone
analysis.2026Implication: With Alwiyah back in BN, traditional base should reconsolidate

analysis.collapse: PH collapsed from 37.8% (2018) to 6.9% (2022) - low turnout + Malay swing to PN + AMANAH candidate (not PKR)
analysis.2026Implication: PH targeting 25% is structurally impossible. Realistic ceiling is 12–15% (requires 2x growth from 2022). Chinese + OA = 18.3% of seat even at 100% turnout. Without 15–20% Malay vote, PH cannot exceed 15%.
analysis.strategicCorrection: CORRECTED (DAF 2026-06-29): PH should focus on 2026 as 'build for 2030' - lock in Chinese base, show up in Malay areas for relationships, accept 12–15% ceiling

turnoutTrend.analysis: Massive turnout drop (23 points) from 2018 to 2022. Low turnout favored incumbent (Alwiyah). 2026 turnout critical: high turnout favors opposition, low turnout favors BN machinery.

demographicContext.note: Electorate relatively stable. Minor decline due to deaths, offset by new voters turning 18.
